summary: Defines the MCP surface: an exported TOOL_DEFINITIONS array holding exactly SIX tools — find, gs, kb_search, kb_lookup, kb_write, kb_status — plus the stdio server wiring. The ListTools handler returns TOOL_DEFINITIONS wholesale with no gating, filtering, or experience/config flag, so the exposed tool count is exactly the array length; kb commit and kb view are deliberately absent (CLI/human-only). TWO SURFACES WITH DIFFERENT TOKEN COSTS, and picking the wrong one is the trap: each tool's `description` is long usage prose that clients load into context EVERY session, whereas the exported SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS string is passed as the SDK's `instructions` option and clients send it ONCE in the initialize result — so setup/lifecycle guidance belongs in SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS and never appended to a tool description. Verified on the wire by piping a raw JSON-RPC initialize into the built server: the result carries `instructions` alongside serverInfo. There is exactly ONE `new Server(` construction site (inside createMcpServer), which startMCPServer routes through, so nothing bypasses it. Note SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS is fixed at construction, before the post-connect roots/list request resolves, so it is necessarily STATIC — it cannot vary on whether the repo already has hooks wired.

summary: MCP server tool registration and handler dispatch. The `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` array (lines 22-197) declares all tools with name, description, and inputSchema (type, properties with type/enum/description, required fields). The `CallToolRequestSchema` handler switch (lines 241-394) dispatches by tool name to individual handlers that call shared engines (find, gs, kb_search, kb_lookup, etc.) and wrap results as `{__rawText?: string}` for text rendering or JSON. New query commands add: one schema entry to TOOL_DEFINITIONS, one case in the switch returning a result object, and a shared engine in find.ts or a new file (e.g., trace.ts).

summary: MCP server tool registration and handler dispatch. TOOL_DEFINITIONS declares every tool (name, description, inputSchema); the CallToolRequestSchema switch dispatches by name to handlers that call shared engines and wrap results as {__rawText} for text or JSON. Adding a query command = one TOOL_DEFINITIONS entry + one case + a shared engine; REMOVING one means both, and the tool description too, since the description is the only place an MCP client learns a section exists. Verified 2026-08-23: unlike the CLI, this server is long-lived, so a sidecar it reads (co-change) must be re-loaded per call — a copy cached at startup goes stale the moment the keeper rewrites it on a branch switch.
